title: Bilal ibn Rabah
hookLine: freed from slavery, the caller to prayer, whose footsteps were heard in the garden (Bukhari)

lines: WHAT DEED DO YOU HOPE IN MOST?
cards: It's the dawn prayer in Medina, still half dark. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, turns to one man with a question.
Bilal, tell me the deed you hope in most, because I heard the sound of your footsteps ahead of me in paradise. This man has come up before. He lay under a rock on the hot sand and said one word: one.
He was bought and set free. His voice called the prayer. And now he's asked: what are you doing that no one sees?
Today begins a new part, the early believers, and Bilal opens it.

teach.b: Start with today's word. A muezzin, in Arabic mu'adhdhin, is the one who gives the adhan, the call to prayer.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Umar tells how the call began in Medina: the companions talked over how to gather people for prayer, and the Prophet said: Bilal, get up and call to the prayer.
So the voice that once said only one, under the rock, became the voice the whole town woke to. That's the public Bilal. The footsteps are about the private one.
The report is in Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah. The Prophet asks, Bilal thinks, and he doesn't name the adhan at all. He says: I have done nothing I hope in more than this.
Whenever I purify myself, by night or by day, I pray with that purification whatever prayer was written for me. That's it.

teach.h: THE DEED: A PRAYER AFTER WUDU.
teach.b: Wudu, the washing before prayer, then a short prayer nobody asked for. A version in the collection of al-Tirmidhi names it as two units. Not a fast, not a well-known act.

A habit done in an empty room, so small no one would think to ask about it. And it was heard in the garden. Muslims may pray a voluntary prayer known as the two units after wudu, and this hadith is behind it.
A man with a very public job pointed to a private thing he did. The voice is what people remembered.
The footsteps are what was heard ahead.

how: In mosques a muezzin gives the adhan before each prayer, and Muslims may pray two short voluntary units after making wudu, often called the sunnah of wudu, following this hadith about Bilal.

s: Bilal named the call to prayer as his best deed
he named a small private habit: praying after each wudu.
the Prophet heard Bilal's footsteps ahead of him in paradise
he asks about it in Bukhari, at the dawn prayer.
the prayer after wudu was something the Prophet ordered him to do
Bilal says he did it on his own, by night or by day.

games.q: you're Bilal. at dawn, the Prophet asks which deed you hope in most. what do you name?
o: the call to prayer, heard across Medina.
holding firm under the rock in Mecca.
the short prayer you pray after every wudu.
games.why: he named the small one: whenever I purify myself, I pray what was written for me. nobody had seen it, and it was heard in the garden.

practice: If you pray, you can do what Bilal did: make wudu, then pray two short units, with nobody asking and nobody watching.
If you don't, wash your hands and face slowly with cool water, then give the next minute to stillness, for no reason anyone else would know.

wordCard.voice: Muezzin. In Arabic, mu'adhdhin: the one who calls the adhan, as Bilal did in Medina. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the one who gives the adhan, the call to prayer; English muezzin comes from it.

carryVoice: Your line: the footsteps of bilal. The quiet deed was the one he named. That's day eight hundred twenty-three.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 604 (Ibn Umar: Bilal, get up and call to the prayer)
